authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from a measured run (script/m14/tmp/make/fixture-dump.mts) and checked against the numbered source: the include on 16, `DEPS` on 19, `EVALUED` on 23, `literal-target` on 27. The fire row is the part_of edge on 16; the three near misses were checked to produce NO part_of edge in the same dump — a count of the dump's part_of rows is 1, and its only line is 16.
rationale: `include` is the textual-inclusion construct: make splices the included file's text into the SAME make instance's scope, which is the single-shared-scope fact `part_of` asserts. The edge's target is the INCLUDED FILE'S MODULE SYMBOL (its basename — the same spelling this analyzer's moduleName() gives every file), never the written path, because the arbiter resolves a target string against symbol names and has no space for a filesystem path; a path target resolves 0 rows. The written path is kept in metadata.partPath where a reader can check it against the source line. Three near misses are pinned as FORBIDS rather than expected absences: `$(shell cat x.mk)` is a command substitution that READS a file without splicing it into this make instance's scope, an `include` inside `$(eval …)` is runtime-generated text this parse sees only as a string, and a commented-out include is a comment node the walk handles as a comment. An expression-target include (`include lib$(ARCH).mk`) is covered by the addIncludePartOf guard's refusal and pinned here as a forbid so the guard cannot be removed silently.
